headword: {縄文|じょうもん}{時代|じだい}

definitions.explanation: The earliest major period of Japanese prehistory, characterized by hunter-gatherer societies and distinctive cord-marked pottery. The name comes from the rope-like patterns ({縄目|なわめ}{文様|もんよう}) pressed into the pottery.

examples.japanese: {縄文|じょうもん}{時代|じだい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{土器|どき}→土器：09658_doki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{発見|はっけん}→発見：00085_hakken⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Pottery from the Jomon period was discovered.

examples.japanese: {縄文|じょうもん}{時代|じだい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人々|ひとびと}→人々：03141_hitobito⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{狩猟|しゅりょう}→狩猟：13507_shuryou⟧⟦{採集|さいしゅう}→採集：00355_saishuu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{生活|せいかつ}していた→生活する：01839_seikatsusuru⟧。
examples.english: People of the Jomon period lived by hunting and gathering.

examples.japanese: ⟦{青森県|あおもりけん}→青森県：28145_aomoriken⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{三内丸山遺跡|さんないまるやまいせき}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{縄文|じょうもん}{時代|じだい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{代表|だいひょう}→代表：03419_daihyou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{遺跡|いせき}→遺跡：09527_iseki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧だ。
examples.english: The Sannai-Maruyama site in Aomori Prefecture is one of the most representative sites of the Jomon period.

notes:
USAGE:
A fundamental term in Japanese history education. The Jomon period is followed by the ⟦{弥生|やよい}{時代|じだい}→弥生時代：20426_yayoijidai⟧ (Yayoi period), which introduced rice farming.

KEY TERMS:
- ⟦{縄文|じょうもん}{土器|どき}→縄文土器：26598_joumondoki⟧: Jomon pottery — the cord-marked pottery that gives the period its name
- ⟦{土偶|どぐう}→土偶：12370_doguu⟧: clay figurine — iconic Jomon artifacts
- ⟦{貝塚|かいづか}→貝塚：28137_kaizuka⟧: shell mound — archaeological sites where Jomon people discarded shells

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{弥生|やよい}{時代|じだい}→弥生時代：20426_yayoijidai⟧: Yayoi period (approx. 300 BCE-300 CE) — the next period, marked by rice cultivation and metalworking
- {旧石器|きゅうせっき}⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧: Paleolithic period — the period before Jomon
